picks.name: Amon-Ra St. Brown
picks.rationale: Ninety percent blended chance at 40+ receiving yards, and both models agree within a few points. Detroit's passing game runs through him, and with Isiah Pacheco now out for the Lions, the offense tilts even further toward the air. New Orleans has no answer for slot receivers of his caliber.

picks.name: Ja'Marr Chase
picks.rationale: An 88% blend for 40+ receiving yards with a healthy Joe Burrow and a Tampa defense that gives up volume to top outside receivers. His target share is the largest in our entire dataset - the safest kind of bet there is.

picks.name: Derrick Henry
picks.rationale: The most reliable rushing floor in football: 92% to clear 40+ on the ground, with Baltimore favored and expected to control the clock. He has cleared this number in all but a handful of games since joining the Ravens.

picks.name: Bijan Robinson
picks.rationale: Ninety percent to clear 40+ rushing yards. Atlanta feeds him regardless of game script, and his receiving work means the touches come even if Pittsburgh stacks the box.

picks.name: Jared Goff
picks.rationale: A 78% chance at 200+ passing yards in a dome against a rebuilding defense, and the Pacheco injury nudges Detroit toward throwing more. Passing props are our most volatile market, so B is the ceiling for week one.

picks.name: Tony Pollard
picks.rationale: The board loves him at 92%, and the volume case is real. We hold at B only because Tennessee's backfield usage in a new season is less proven than the tier-A names above.

picks.name: Ashton Jeanty
picks.rationale: The model has believed in Jeanty's workload since his rookie year and gives him 88% here. Second-year backs with a full offseason as the starter are usually safe - B only because Miami's speed can tilt games into passing scripts.

picks.name: Lamar Jackson
picks.rationale: The number says 79% for 200+ passing yards, but our O-line health tracker flags Baltimore's pass protection, and when the Ravens are comfortable they simply stop throwing. Watch list, not a bet.

passes.name: Wan'Dale Robinson
passes.reason: The board has him at 89% on pure volume, but Malik Nabers is returning from his ACL and the Giants' target distribution is about to change in ways our model cannot see yet. Classic trap: great historical numbers, changed circumstances.

passes.name: Daniel Jones / Philip Rivers (IND passing)
passes.reason: Indianapolis has an unresolved quarterback battle - our model splits its confidence across two different starters. Until one is named, any Colts passing prop is a coin flip wearing a costume.
